annotations.description: 1.02 checkpoint(s) failed in the last 10 minutes.

diagnosis.summary: Flink checkpoint failures were triggered by a task manager pod restart ~2 minutes ago (TaskExecutor shutdown event). The job is already recovering: RUNNING/STABLE with ~25 completed checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. Chaos Mesh deployments active in this window are the likely cause of repeated disruptions.
diagnosis.root_cause: The task manager pod `events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2` was restarted (pod age: 1.9 min, 0 restarts on new pod), causing the in-flight checkpoint to fail. The Kubernetes event confirms `org.apache.flink.util.FlinkExpectedException: The TaskExecutor is shutting down` 1.9 minutes ago. The Flink operator recovered the job automatically from its latest checkpoint: the job is now RUNNING/STABLE (uptime 96 s) and completing ~25 checkpoints per 5-minute window as expected (every ~12 s). The root trigger appears to be Chaos Mesh activity — chaos-mesh-local was deployed at least 4 times in the last 45 minutes, and a prior chaos-mesh revision (9187ff9e9e6f) deployed 144.6 min ago coincides exactly with the mass pod terminations (exit_code 255) across Kafka brokers, the Flink jobmanager, and the ingestion service ~140.9 min ago.
diagnosis.impact: The Flink streaming pipeline experienced ~2 failed checkpoints over ~2 minutes, meaning exactly-once delivery guarantees were briefly at risk. The job has since recovered and is writing to Iceberg again (last commit 2 min ago). Consumer lag stands at 650 messages and should drain quickly. No data loss expected given recovery from last good checkpoint. Secondary concern: 146/146 Iceberg data files are below the 32 MiB small-file threshold, requiring compaction.

evidence.finding: Job RUNNING/STABLE, uptime 96 s, 1.018 restarts in last 15 min, 2.104 failed checkpoints in last 10 min, but 24.995 completed checkpoints in last 5 min — actively recovering. Consumer lag 650. Task manager pod age: 1.9 min.
Warning JobException on FlinkDeployment/events-to-iceberg 1.9 min ago: 'The TaskExecutor is shutting down' — confirms task manager forced-stop triggered checkpoint failure.
events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 is 1.9 min old, 0 restarts (newly scheduled pod). Jobmanager last terminated 140.9 min ago with exit_code 255 (Unknown).
All 3 Kafka brokers Running/Ready, 0 under-replicated or offline partitions, 1 active controller. Brokers also terminated with exit_code 255 ~140.9 min ago. Kafka itself is healthy now.
chaos-mesh-local deployed 4 times in last 45 min (revisions 47886843, c702990f, 496cc7deaf72, 9187ff9e9e6f). Deployment at 144.6 min ago aligns with mass pod terminations at 140.9 min ago.
All 3 worker nodes Ready, no pressure conditions, no cordons. Node failure is not a factor.
lakehouse.events: 146/146 data files are small (<32 MiB), 776 snapshots, last compaction 3.8 h ago. Secondary maintenance issue.

proposed_action.rationale: The Flink job has already self-healed: operator shows RUNNING/STABLE, checkpoints are completing every ~12 s, and the Iceberg table received a commit 2 min ago. Restarting the job would force a full checkpoint cycle from scratch and is unnecessary. The consumer lag of 650 messages is small and will drain on its own. Iceberg compaction is a separate maintenance concern and can be scheduled independently.

follow_ups: Investigate active Chaos Mesh experiments: 4+ deployments in 45 min suggest an experiment is intentionally killing pods. Confirm whether this is planned chaos testing; if not, suspend chaos-mesh immediately.

Run Iceberg compaction on lakehouse.events: 146/146 files are small-files, last compaction 3.8 h ago — this will degrade query performance if left unaddressed (run_iceberg_compaction action available).
Monitor consumer lag (currently 650) over the next 10 minutes to confirm it drains back to 0 as expected.

Audit why multiple pods across namespaces (Kafka brokers, Flink jobmanager, ingestion-service) all terminated with exit_code 255 ~140.9 min ago — confirm this was the previous Chaos Mesh experiment and check for any data integrity impact.
Review Flink exactly-once guarantees: with 2 failed checkpoints during the restart window, verify no duplicate or missing records were written to Iceberg around the incident time.
